summary: cro checked in 1 executive handoff item(s)

items.summary:
Recommend no new implementation or adoption this cycle; retain the following evidence-backed opportunities for CEO/CTO review after current measurement, ownership, security, attribution, and failure-repair gates clear.

1) allthingsmasonic.com affiliate CTA experiment. Evidence: 61 Amazon clicks, 0 attributed orders, and $0 site-attributed commission in the available 2026-09-21 window; public inspection documented CTA, destination, disclosure, and accessibility evidence. Smallest reversible prototype: one existing merchandising surface with clearer product relevance, CTA copy, and disclosure placement. Metric: affiliate click-through and site-attributed ordered items; time-to-learn: 14 days or 100 relevant impressions/clicks. Risks: aggregate attribution is partial, product/link freshness is unknown, and no revenue lift may be claimed before measurement. Rollback: revert the single surface.

2) deeppenetrations.com search-to-affiliate intent test. Evidence: /reviews/liquid-wrench had 99 impressions at position 2.8 with 0 clicks; /reviews/wd40-silicone had 140 impressions at position 4.9 with 0 clicks; the existing snippet improvement is already measuring. Smallest next prototype after the active run closes: one comparison block linking only to existing, verified destinations. Metric: organic CTR, affiliate outbound clicks, and attributed orders where available; time-to-learn: 14 days or 100 relevant impressions. Risks: active work, low session volume, attribution lag, and security/operations evidence gaps. Do not duplicate the active improvement.

3) reusable accessible CTA/comparison-card capability. Evidence: bounded inspection of 0xroulette.com supports a CTA-hierarchy hypothesis; existing lab evidence supports shadcn-ui/ui for composable accessible components, MIT license, 3 bounded checks passed, no dependency installation, and no production access. Smallest prototype: static, dependency-free card markup in one preview only. Metric: CTA engagement and destination integrity using existing telemetry; time-to-learn: 14 days after deployment. Risks: repository maintenance and transitive dependency posture remain unverified; require CTO/security review and license scan before adoption. Rollback: remove the isolated component.

4) offline content-structure experiment. Evidence: microsoft/markitdown is MIT, 8/8 bounded checks passed, and documentation supports document-to-Markdown conversion; mermaid-js/mermaid is MIT with supported SEO-content fit but no native checks available without dependencies. Smallest prototype: offline conversion of one owned source document into a draft outline plus one internal diagram, with no publishing or new dependency. Metric: editor acceptance time and publish-ready draft quality, not traffic or revenue; time-to-learn: 1 working session. Risks: source rights, factual accuracy, maintenance, dependency and supply-chain review remain unknown. Keep research-only.

Do not deploy, spend, change credentials, add domains, add telemetry, install dependencies, or expand monetization. Preserve all opportunities as deferred CRO backlog until existing gates clear; do not infer revenue, ROI, causal lift, or repository quality from stars or lab evidence alone.
